items.title: Finite-time quantum equilibration from local correlations
items.summary: An isolated quantum system evolves reversibly, yet a small subsystem can lose nearly all information about its initial state. Conserved quantities may retain some of this information, depending on how strongly they overlap with local observables. Here we consider a subsystem in an arbitrary initial state coupled to a maximally mixed bath. We show that the worst-input mean-square equilibration error, maximised over window origins, is bounded from above and below by the mean square of a complete local autocorrelation, with the stationary part subtracted. The two mean-square quantities are linearly comparable. A correlation record over a finite interval therefore controls the equilibration error in every interval of the same length, and the result extends to nonnegative observation weights with nonnegative Fourier transform. The result allows arbitrary degeneracies of energies and gaps. We apply it to two static Hamiltonian families. For fixed spin subsystems in the one-particle sector of a bounded-range periodic clock, fixed-accuracy thermalisation is guaranteed on windows that grow only slightly faster than linearly with system size, despite exponentially small positive energies. A random commuting model with logarithmic interaction range retains an extensive set of conserved observables. Its expected mean-square error is bounded by a finite-size term and an inverse-time term. The inverse-time dependence is unavoidable because of the initial transient. These examples show how local relaxation can coexist with exact conservation laws and a finely spaced spectrum.

items.title: Pseudomagnetic focusing of valley-polarized beams in strained graphene
items.summary: In addition to spin, the low-energy charge carriers in graphene have two inequivalent valley flavors K and K' related by time-reversal symmetry, which can potentially serve as carriers for additional information. One promising route of controlling the valley degree of freedom relies on strain-induced pseudomagnetic fields, which couple with opposite signs to the two valleys. In this work, we theoretically investigate quantum transport in strained graphene devices that host tailored pseudomagnetic field profiles for valley manipulation. We focus on experimentally feasible geometries and propose transverse pseudomagnetic focusing in a bent graphene ribbon as an efficient method for generating valley-polarized currents, even in presence of disorder. Our work highlights pseudomagneto-transport in graphene as a viable tool for valleytronic applications.

items.title: Binder migration across film consolidation and pore emptying in electrode drying: a continuous model validated against drying-rate, thickness, and schedule experiments
items.summary: Drying battery electrodes faster saves energy but drives dissolved binder toward the film surface, depleting the current-collector interface and weakening adhesion. Models of this migration stop convecting the binder when film consolidation ends, and models of the subsequent pore emptying omit the binder or start from an assumed binder field, so no simulation has followed binder convection through both stages that a drying schedule acts on. This study presents a continuous simulation of the dissolved binder field across both stages, driven by the published drying rates and completed by effective descriptions of the two questions the base transport physics leaves open: where the liquid of the consolidating film carries the binder, and when the binder stops moving as the pores empty. With a single parameter set, the simulation reproduces three types of published measurements: the change of the surface-to-interface binder ratio with drying rate over a factor of 5.6 and the surface and interface binder levels of films six times thicker; concentration profiles through the film interior; and the response of the interface binder to the time at which the drying rate is switched mid-process. Applied without further adjustment to a published three-stage schedule, the model reproduces the shortened drying and the full interface recovery when the rate is lowered early, and shows that its final high-rate stage begins after the binder has stopped. Combined with a coater-scale process model, the model can be used to identify operating points for electrode production that improve energy efficiency and product quality together.

items.title: Chirality, Klein duality, and the stability of Kitaev spin liquids on the star lattice
items.summary: The star lattice hosts the Yao-Kivelson chiral spin liquid, an exactly solvable Kitaev spin liquid that breaks time reversal spontaneously and is non-Abelian or Abelian depending on the ratio of its two couplings. A density-matrix renormalization group study found that an added Heisenberg exchange leaves it a wide stability window for ferromagnetic but only a narrow one for antiferromagnetic Kitaev coupling. Using projective symmetry groups (PSGs) of fermionic partons, we show that the chirality is not a peculiarity of the solvable point: whenever the $π$ spin rotations act on the partons as in the exact solution (spin-gauge locking), a time-reversal-symmetric mean-field state has no amplitude on the triangles, at any range, so a Kitaev-type spin liquid on this lattice must break time reversal. The Abelian and non-Abelian liquids of both signs share a single chiral PSG, within which their transition is a band inversion. The Klein duality, which reverses the Heisenberg coupling, permutes the PSGs and leaves exactly the locked ones unchanged; a $Z_2$ spin-liquid phase mapped onto itself is therefore locked and, if it spans a connected range of couplings, contains a Kitaev point. Unprojected mean-field theory in Kitaev's Majorana representation treats both signs alike. Exact second-order perturbation theory about the Kitaev points locates the asymmetry: the triangles respond identically for both signs, whereas on the bonds between triangles the two off-diagonal Heisenberg terms create the same four visons and interfere constructively for antiferromagnetic and almost destructively for ferromagnetic coupling, admixing a low-energy four-vison state $82$ times more strongly on the antiferromagnetic side. The PSG results rest on a classification of $352$ $Z_2$ PSGs with spin-orbit-coupled amplitudes, which also identifies the fermionic partners of the known Schwinger-boson spin liquids.

items.title: Interplay of disorder and phonons in two-dimensional transport
items.summary: We calculate the temperature- and density-dependent resistivity of bilayer MoSe$_2$ in the presence of charged impurities, short-range defects, and longitudinal acoustic phonons, using the Boltzmann transport theory with screening treated in the random phase approximation, and compare the results with recent transport measurements. The disorder parameters are taken from the experiment itself and the phonon parameters are taken from literature estimates for MoSe$_2$. We find that screened acoustic phonons are a small correction to the disorder-limited resistivity over the entire experimental temperature range, so that the temperature dependence of the measured resistivity on the metallic side is controlled by the temperature-dependent screening of charged disorder and by neutral defects. We also show that a resistivity minimum as a function of temperature can arise on both sides of the metal-insulator crossover through two different mechanisms: on the insulating side from the interplay between activated carriers and resistive scattering, and on the metallic side from the interplay between disorder and phonon scattering. The existence of a resistivity minimum by itself therefore does not identify the phase.

items.title: Precipitation strengthening as a collective multi-dislocation phenomenon
items.summary: Precipitation strengthening is a cornerstone of physical metallurgy, delivering otherwise unattainable combinations of strength and ductility. The approach relies on nanoscale precipitates that impede the motion of dislocations, the primary carriers of metal plasticity. Historically, precipitation strengthening has been rationalized via two idealized, limiting mechanisms: dislocations either cut through or bow around precipitates. However, under many technologically relevant conditions, multiple dislocations can interact with a precipitate at the same time, potentially giving rise to distinct precipitate-dislocation dynamics that in situ experiments are yet to fully resolve. Here, using large-scale atomistic simulations (100 million atoms) that capture these dynamics, we demonstrate that in this regime, the cutting-versus-bowing dichotomy is incomplete: strengthening arises as an emergent phenomenon driven by concurrent multi-dislocation interactions. These interactions simultaneously induce dislocation accumulation at interfaces, storage within precipitates, and precipitate-mediated multiplication inside the matrix. Our findings establish a distinct mechanistic regime of precipitation strengthening beyond traditional models and provide a quantitative foundation for predicting its behavior.

items.title: Higher-Order Flatband-Touching Points Mediate Unconventional Bulk-Boundary Correspondence
items.summary: The bulk-boundary correspondence establishes a fundamental connection between bulk band topology and the emergence of boundary states, underpinning topological phenomena across electronic, acoustic, photonic, and many other wave systems. A broad class of singular flatband systems, however, exhibits an unconventional form of bulk-boundary correspondence, in which robust boundary modes (RBMs) originate from flatband-touching points (FBTPs) and the real-space topology associated with incomplete sets of compact localized states (CLSs), rather than conventional momentum-space bulk topological invariants. To date, experimental studies of such boundary modes have been limited to systems hosting lower-order FBTPs. Here, we experimentally demonstrate unconventional bulk-boundary correspondence in a photonic cross-bedded Kagome-like lattice featuring a higher-order FBTP formed by the touching of two degenerate flatbands and a dispersive band. Using continuous-wave laser writing, we observe shape-preserving propagation of both bulk CLSs and boundary RBMs. Remarkably, unlike previously reported flatband systems, the RBMs retain their boundary localization under input-field perturbations involving both singular and nonsingular CLSs, revealing an unconventional boundary response associated with the higher-order FBTP in this lattice. Our results establish the Kagome-like lattice as a new platform for exploring flatband physics and unconventional bulk-boundary correspondence, with potential applications in wave localization, flatband lasers, and other emerging topological photonic devices.

items.title: Structural signatures of a topological transition in a disordered tetrahedral network
items.summary: Topological transitions in disordered network materials are often characterised using descriptors of entanglement, such as ring linking and writhe, which can be difficult to access experimentally. Here we investigate whether a topological transition can instead be identified using structural descriptors more readily connected to experiment. We reanalyse configurations of a colloidal tetrahedral network model known to exhibit a pressure-driven transition between unentangled and and entangled states. We show that the cumulative all-rings vertex symbol (CARVS), a descriptor of medium-range network topology based on ring statistics, provides a clear signature of this transition despite containing no explicit information about ring linking. We further show that network entanglement produces characteristic changes in the radial distribution function and structure factor, including the emergence of short-range correlations between nonbonded nodes and the disappearance of a low-angle scattering pre-peak. These results establish experimentally accessible structural signatures of topological transitions in disordered tetrahedral networks. Comparison with canonical continuous random networks further suggests that framework materials with extended linkers may provide promising candidate systems in which to search experimentally for entanglement-driven topological transitions.

items.title: Disorder-Mediated Magnetism in Transition-Metal Dichalcogenide Monolayers: XS$_2$ and XSe$_2$ (X = Ti, V, Co, Mo, and Ru)
items.summary: Magnetism in transition-metal dichalcogenide monolayers has attracted considerable attention, yet its nature remains elusive, particularly in monolayer 1T-VSe$_2$. Our first-principles calculations show that Stoner instability can drive ferromagnetism in XS$_2$ and XSe$_2$ monolayers (X = Ti, V, Co, Mo, and Ru), associated with a reduced density of states at the Fermi level. We demonstrate that mixing nonmagnetic Ti, Co, Mo, and Ru disulfides or diselenides can induce magnetism. Conversely, mixing magnetic VS$_2$ or VSe$_2$ with other compounds can completely suppress magnetism. Both scenarios can lower the total energy. Moreover, substituting a small number of V atoms with Co defects can also disrupt ferromagnetism in 1T-V(S,Se)$_2$. Even in pristine 1T-VSe$_2$, we find ferrimagnetic configurations with reversed local V moments that are nearly degenerate with the ferromagnetic state. Their competition may contribute to the suppression of long-range ferromagnetic order. This reduced energy penalty for magnetic and structural disorder arises from a suppressed density of states at the Fermi level, resembling the mechanism underlying the Peierls transition. Electronically driven energy lowering near the Fermi level may therefore be widespread among transition-metal dichalcogenide monolayers in various forms.

items.title: Geometry-controlled zeros of resonant Kelvin-wave conversion in four spatial dimensions
items.summary: Kelvin waves carry energy along vortices, but their resonant interactions contain information that is absent from the linear spectrum. We identify a geometry that exposes this information on a vortex surface in four spatial dimensions. Perpendicular incoming waves cancel the complete local-area four-wave coupling, leaving the finite nonlocal interaction mediated by the surrounding fluid. This interaction restores conversion at generic wave-number ratios, yet changes sign and vanishes at a selected ratio while momentum and frequency remain exactly matched. Matching to Gross-Pitaevskii (GP) theory, including the microscopic core response, establishes a zero of the full coupling at every sufficiently small nonzero wave number, with ratio tending to $λ_*\simeq1.469$. Finite-grid GP coefficients exhibit a sign reversal for the same resonant quartets. Separate coherent-mixing calculations and weak-probe spectra connect the coupling sign to the generated-wave phase and the ordering of reflection-even and reflection-odd modes. The resulting suppression removes a leading channel for changing propagation directions without changing the paired wavelengths. These results isolate a nonlinear effect of the surrounding flow that local tension misses, providing a microscopic benchmark for vortex-wave theories and a starting point for studying angular redistribution beyond the Kelvin spectrum.

items.title: Mixed-State Topology in One-Dimensional Open Floquet Systems
items.summary: We investigate the non-equilibrium topology of the steady state of a periodically driven, dissipative Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain using the ensemble geometric phase (EGP) $φ_{\mathrm{EGP}}$, a generalisation of the Zak phase to mixed states. The coupling to thermal reservoirs is treated microscopically within Floquet-Born-Markov theory without the rotating-wave approximation. We classify the steady state rather than the generator of the dynamics, using its purity spectrum as the analogue of a band structure. We show that, within the EGP framework, the $\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}$ structure of isolated chiral-symmetric Floquet SSH systems generally does not carry over to the steady state. Instead, the steady state carries a single invariant whose type is set by an underlying symmetry. When this symmetry holds, the invariant is $\mathbb{Z}_2$-valued, with quantised $φ_{\mathrm{EGP}}=\pmπ/2$ at all times and finite temperatures. The EGP can switch within a driving period, tracking the presence of edge modes in the open-boundary purity spectrum and thereby establishing a bulk-boundary correspondence. The fraction of each period spent in the nontrivial regime varies continuously with the driving frequency, and the switching disappears if the dependence of the dissipator on the drive is neglected. When the symmetry is broken, $φ_{\mathrm{EGP}}$ is no longer quantised, but its winding over a drive period $T$ defines an invariant $ν_T \in \mathbb Z$, with no purity-spectrum bulk-boundary correspondence. We propose that its changes signal temperature- and frequency-driven topological phase transitions. Our formalism extends to general quadratic fermionic systems with linear bath couplings.

items.title: Valence-Driven Structural Transformation and Phase Coexistence in Chemically Substituted EuPd2Si2
items.summary: EuPd2Si2 serves as an ideal system to probe the interplay between lattice dynamics and electronic instabilities through its tunable valence transition, responsive to temperature, pressure, and magnetic field. Here, we focus on investigating the origin of the temperature-induced europium valence instability in pristine EuPd2Si2, alloyed EuPd2Si1.95Ge0.05, and EuPd2Si1.9Ge0.1 and its correlation with structural responses. Compared with the parent compound EuPd2Si2 which exhibits the europium valence transition at Tv = 143 K, magnetic susceptibility measurements reveal a systematic shift in Tv with Ge substitution, decreasing to 87 K for EuPd2Si1.95Ge0.05. Temperature-dependent synchrotron X-ray diffraction confirms phase coexistence between Eu2+Pd2Si2-xGex and Eu3+Pd2Si2-xGex phases across the valence transition for all samples measured (x = 0, 0.05, 0.10). The pronounced increase in the full width at half maximum (FWHM) well above Tv reflects the gradual nature of the transformation and highlights the role of structural strain in stabilizing the coexisting phases, supporting the presence of a phase-segregated ground state, in contrast to a homogeneous intermediate-valence or mixed-valence state. The variation in Tv across different compositions correlates with changes in lattice parameters, highlighting the robust coupling between the structural and electronic degrees of freedom. The phase diagram suggests an inverse linear relationship between the lattice parameter and Tv, suggesting a possible predictive framework for estimating transition temperatures in other chemically substituted variants of this family.

items.title: Numerical Prediction of NaCl Solubility in Water Using the TIP4P/05 Water Model NaCl/Madrid
items.summary: The solid-liquid equilibrium and solubility of NaCl in water were investigated using molecular dynamics simulations with the NaCl/Madrid force field and the TIP4P/05 water model. Particular attention was given to the influence of the intermolecular cut-off radius, rcut, used to identify ions belonging to the crystalline phase. Simulations were initiated from a NaCl crystal immersed in an aqueous NaCl solution, following the configuration proposed by Manzanilla-Granados et al. After equilibration, the system was analysed over an extended simulation trajectory. The radial distribution function, g(r), was used to establish a physically motivated criterion for distinguishing the crystalline and aqueous phases. Specifically, the first minimum following the principal Na-Cl correlation peak was used to characterise the ionic coordination environment and constrain the range of meaningful cut-off radii. The number of ions remaining in the crystalline phase was then evaluated as a function of rcut, allowing the corresponding solubility to be estimated. The resulting curve exhibits a well-defined inflection point, providing a criterion for identifying the transition between predominantly crystalline and dissolved ionic populations. This approach offers a structural basis for determining NaCl solubility directly from the evolution of the solid-liquid system, avoiding the arbitrary selection of the cut-off distance. The results demonstrate that combining radial distribution functions with cut-off-dependent analysis provides a useful framework for characterising solid-liquid behaviour and estimating the solubility of ionic crystals through molecular dynamics simulations.

items.title: Numerical study of the free energy monotonicity for the Enskog equation: The thermal relaxation of the dense gas between two parallel plates
items.summary: The thermal relaxation problem between two parallel plates with the same temperature is investigated, aiming to study the behavior of the free energy of the dense gas described by the Enskog equation. Two types of Enskog equation have been used: one is the Enskog equation with the original Enskog factor, while the other is that with a modified Enskog factor proposed recently in Takata \& Takahashi, Phys. Rev. E \textbf{111}, 065108 (2025). The evaluated free energy is a natural extension of the thermodynamic free energy to the non-equilibrium state. It is observed that this free energy monotonically decreases in time for the modified factor version, while it is not necessarily the case for the original version. Differences are also observed in other quantities in the time evolution, most typically in the density profile.

items.title: Fast and Sensitive Readout of a Semiconductor Quantum Dot Using an In-Situ Microwave Resonator with Enhanced Gate Lever Arm
items.summary: We report an experimental study of a Si/SiGe double quantum dot (DQD) directly coupled to a niobium superconducting coplanar stripline (CPS) microwave resonator. This hybrid architecture enables high-bandwidth dispersive readout suitable for real-time feedback and error-correction protocols. Fast and sensitive readout is achieved primarily by optimizing the DQD gate lever arm, guided by MaSQE quantum dot simulations, which enhances the dispersive signal without requiring high-impedance resonators. We demonstrate a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of unity with an integration time of 34.54 nanoseconds, corresponding to a system bandwidth of 14.48 MHz and a charge sensitivity of 0.000186 e per square root hertz. Analysis of the voltage power spectral density (PSD) of the in-phase (I) and quadrature (Q) baseband signals characterizes the system's readout noise, with the PSD's dependence on integration time providing insight into distinct physical regimes.

items.title: JANUS: A Multi-modal Foundation Neural Sampler for Disordered Materials
items.summary: Disordered materials are central to modern technologies, from high-performance alloys to quantum devices, yet understanding and designing them requires exploring an enormous space of compositions and atomic arrangements. Here we introduce JANUS, a multimodal neural sampler that jointly explores chemical composition, atomic structure and volume, learning directly from the energy of the system without requiring pre-generated equilibrium configurations. Across test systems, JANUS reproduces reference equilibrium properties and recovers free energy and phase behavior with about three orders of magnitude fewer energy evaluations than reference Monte Carlo sampling. In multicomponent alloys, JANUS reproduces experimentally observed local chemical order and can be steered to further enhance chemical order and stiffness. Coupled to an evolutionary language model agent, it also enables efficient design of alloys with balanced optical and mechanical properties. Beyond alloys, JANUS explores vacancies and dopants spanning 15 elements in semiconductors including silicon and diamond, recovers established defects including the silicon $E$ centre, and identifies new candidate defect pairs and triplets for quantum engineering, including S-Ti in silicon and B-[O]-O in diamond, with deep in-gap states validated by hybrid-functional density functional theory. By unifying exploration across composition, atomic arrangement and volume, JANUS opens a new avenue for understanding, characterizing and designing chemically disordered materials.

items.title: Magnetization and Josephson current coupling drives the Josephson diode effect in FeTe0.55Se0.45 van der Waals junctions
items.summary: The Josephson diode effect (JDE) reflects symmetry breaking in the current-phase relation (CPR) of Josephson junctions, yet establishing its microscopic origin is often challenging. We investigate the mechanism of the JDE in van der Waals Josephson junctions based on FeTe0.55Se0.45, a platform where superconductivity, topology, and magnetism may coexist at the interface. Our devices exhibit a robust zero-field diode response with asymmetric switching currents. Magnetic-field measurements reveal a hysteretic Fraunhofer pattern and magnetic-resonance-induced voltage feature, evidencing interfacial magnetism coupled to the Josephson current. Microwave response further shows half-integer Shapiro steps with asymmetric evolution, demonstrating contributions from both a second harmonic and a magnetization-induced phase shift in CPR. Numerical simulations combining magnetization dynamics and Josephson phase dynamics reproduce these features, confirming that the JDE originates from interfacial coupling between magnetization and Josephson current. This work provides a transport-based route to pinpoint the microscopic mechanism of the JDE, establishing a platform for exploring magnetically active interfacial superconductivity, and enables the design of nonreciprocal superconducting devices in clean, interface-engineered van der Waals systems.

items.title: Geometry and electronic properties of chiral phosphorene nanotubes
items.summary: Phosphorene nanotubes (PNTs) exhibit highly tunable electronic properties, yet research has largely focused on high-symmetry armchair and zigzag configurations. This work presents the first systematic study of the geometric and electronic properties of chiral PNTs. Using the Chiraltube software, a comprehensive set of 214 PNTs was generated and analyzed via a 2D zone-folding mapping approach. Subsequently, a representative subset of 48 chiral PNTs was selected for ab initio calculations covering the full chiral space. While the mapping method overestimates band gaps by directly inheriting monolayer features, it serves as a qualitative tool for specific chiral geometries-particularly armchair configurations and larger-radius tubes-by effectively capturing their subband density and dispersion profiles. Finally, this work details the evolution of structural stability and electronic properties as a function of radius and chirality, identifying clear direct-to-indirect band gap transitions driven by curvature effects, alongside metallic behavior in specific zigzag configurations.

items.title: Symmetry-Guided Machine Learning of Spin-Dependent Nonlinear Hall Response
items.summary: A Berry-curvature dipole can produce a nonlinear Hall current even when the linear Hall response vanishes, but symmetry alone does not determine its magnitude or magnetic tunability. The interplay of structural symmetry, moment orientation, and carrier occupation is examined in a honeycomb model. Curvature maps and the band-summed dipole integrand reveal how velocity and the occupation window near the Fermi level select signed contributions. Removing threefold rotation permits a nonmagnetic dipole perpendicular to the surviving mirror. Generic magnetic reorientation activates the second component and tunes both components through positive and negative values. Global reversal preserves the dipole while reversing the intrinsic linear Hall conductivity, allowing a finite bulk dipole contribution from equally populated reversed domains under uniform-field averaging.A symmetry-constrained polynomial model predicts both dipole components for 256 held-out spin configurations, achieving coefficients of determination $R^2 > 0.9995$ at the reference chemical potential. At fixed carrier density, orientation-dependent shifts of the chemical potential modify the response and yield slightly larger prediction errors for the chosen model. Across the chemical-potential sweep,the prediction accuracy decreases more strongly for $D_y$,revealing an energy dependence of the surrogate's performance. Within semiclassical transport with a constant relaxation time, the calculated dipole determines the angular dependence of the quadratic current and its rectified and second-harmonic components. These results provide a quantitative representation of magnetic-orientation-dependent Berry-curvature dipoles and show how carrier occupation influences both the response and its predictability.

items.title: Algebraic criteria for complete relaxation in autonomous and periodically driven open quantum systems
items.summary: We derive sufficient criteria that guarantee convergence of open quantum system dynamics to a unique long-time state independent of the initial conditions. We refer to this behavior as complete relaxation. Focusing on systems described by Gorini-Kossakowski-Sudarshan-Lindblad (GKSL) master equations on finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, our approach uses only elementary mathematical arguments. For autonomous systems, we recover three previously derived relaxation criteria, which can be expressed as algebraic conditions on the Lindblad operators and the Hamiltonian entering the GKSL equation. For periodically driven systems, we obtain a new criterion involving a similar algebraic condition and a local continuity requirement on the time-dependent GKSL generator. This result implies an earlier criterion for complete relaxation formulated in Ref. [J. Phys. A 52, 43LT01 (2019)]. We also discuss implications of our approach for periodically modulated classical master equations, as well as extensions to driven systems without a periodicity constraint.

items.title: Quantitative Eshelby stability: local and finite-shape theory through AI-assisted mechanics
items.summary: How can human researchers use artificial intelligence (AI) to make progress on difficult mechanics problems while retaining control of physical significance, mathematical rigor, and validation? We explore this opportunity through a quantitative stability problem rooted in the Eshelby conjecture. For a uniform dilatational eigenstrain in a homogeneous isotropic solid, we establish a nonlinear two-sided relation between whole-interior strain heterogeneity and a geometry-only distance from the ellipsoid family, with half-order Sobolev scaling that captures morphological length scale. We then develop a complementary finite-shape theory: ellipsoidal subtraction yields an exact residual-field budget from which systematically convergent upper and lower bounds are obtained for a prescribed geometry. Applied to protruded, indented, and necked inclusions, the bounds agree with independent displacement-based finite-element calculations. The study also documents a human-led, AI-assisted research process in which researchers select consequential problems, shape targets, audit arguments, require independent checks, and interpret mechanics, while AI broadens analytical exploration and supports computation. This experience also led us to develop Open Problems in Mechanics, a versioned community-facing map that makes selected mechanics questions, their known/open boundaries, and criteria for progress explicit.

items.title: The Spectroscopic Atlas of Excitonic Complexes in hBN-Encapsulated S-TMD Monolayers: From Excitons to Oxcitons and Beyond
items.summary: Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) encapsulation has transformed the optical spectroscopy of semiconducting transition-metal dichalcogenide monolayers (MLs) by suppressing extrinsic disorder and enabling the resolution of an increasingly complex hierarchy of excitonic states. This Review provides a spectroscopy-oriented framework for understanding and identifying excitonic complexes in hBN-encapsulated Mo- and W-based MLs and their alloys. The discussion covers bright and dark excitons, Rydberg states, charged excitons, biexcitons, phonon-assisted replicas, and higher-order Fermi-sea many-body states, including hexcitons and oxcitons, with an emphasis on the experimental signatures that distinguish them. Particular attention is given to the combined use of photoluminescence and absorption-related spectroscopy, electrostatic gating, polarization analysis, excitation-power and temperature dependences, magnetic fields, and time-resolved measurements to establish microscopic assignments. The role of alloying as an additional degree of freedom for engineering the excitonic hierarchy, spin-valley configuration, and magneto-optical response is also highlighted. By organizing the rapidly expanding phenomenology around experimentally accessible fingerprints rather than individual material systems, this Review aims to provide a practical and broadly applicable guide for identifying, comparing, and engineering excitonic states in high-quality two-dimensional semiconductors.

items.title: A Combined Tight Binding with Machine Learning Potential Model for Magnesium Compounds
items.summary: We present a model for magnesium-based systems that combines density functional tight binding (DFTB) with MACE, a machine learning interatomic potential (DFTB+MACE). In this model, the conventional repulsive potential, pair potential, is replaced by a many-body MACE potential. The MACE component of the model is trained on the difference between density functional theory (DFT) energies and forces and the corresponding DFTB values, but neglecting the pair potential contribution. Using this model we performed structural relaxation of MgO-CO2 adsorption systems, molecular dynamics calculations of water clusters and phonon spectrum calculations of stable fcc-MgO and metastable bcc-MgO structures. We compare the performance of our model with a pure MACE model and with DFT. We demonstrate that the DFTB+MACE model achieves improved accuracy relative to DFTB with a pair potential, in many cases with only a moderate increase in computational cost. In addition, it can provide electronic structures that most of the machine learning potentials cannot. The training dataset, originally developed for MACE, may not fully represent all regions of the potential surface we may encounter during simulations. Expanding the dataset for a wider potential surface is expected to further enhance predictive accuracy of DFTB+MACE model. Overall, the resulting DFTB+MACE framework enables simulations at length and time scales beyond the reach of first-principles methods while retaining an explicit description of electronic structures, making it particularly attractive for studying charge-transfer in materials.

items.title: Exotic vortex states and enhancement of orbital upper critical fields in an $s$-wave quasicrystalline superconductor
items.summary: Quasicrystals possess long-range order without translational symmetry, giving rise to intrinsically inhomogeneous superconducting states. Using the Bogoliubov-de Gennes mean-field theory, we investigate vortex states in an $s$-wave quasicrystalline superconductor on the Ammann-Beenker tiling, with particular emphasis on the high-field regime. We find that the vortex configuration can differ qualitatively from the Abrikosov triangular lattice. In particular, at filling $ν=0.8$, vortices preferentially penetrate weak-pairing regions centered on sites with coordination number $8$, indicating that their spatial organization is strongly influenced by the local geometry. Furthermore, we observe an enhanced upper critical field. At $ν=0.8$, where the enhancement is particularly pronounced, the spatially averaged order parameter exhibits a plateau-like field dependence accompanied by the formation of vortex clusters. These clusters accommodate additional flux in locally weak superconducting regions, providing a microscopic interpretation of the plateau-like behavior. Moreover, the upper critical field increases upon cooling toward zero temperature without a clear sign of saturation.

items.title: Dynamics of self-organization in dense persistent active matter
items.summary: We consider a two-dimensional athermal binary mixture of Lennard-Jones particles with persistent random active forces. The liquid phase of this system for active forces exceeding a threshold value exhibits self-organization with long-range spatial correlations of particle velocities and active forces. We study by simulations the development of these correlations from a random initial state. Several characteristics of the growth of correlations are measured and compared with those of phase-ordering kinetics of equilibrium systems after a quench from a disordered state. The motion of the particles in the long-time steady state is found to be dominated by two streams that flow in opposite directions.

items.title: Ubiquitous topological materials protected by hidden partial symmetries
items.summary: Symmetries play a crucial role in protecting the topological phases of insulators, ensuring the robustness of their surface states against perturbations. Traditionally, these symmetries have to be obeyed by the system as a whole, which is a rather strong constraint. In this work, we demonstrate that topological effects can also be realized through a substantially weaker form of symmetry that we coin \emph{partial latent symmetries}. For these, invariance is required only at certain energy scales of an effective Hamiltonian, rather than for the object as a whole. Applying this idea, we construct weak-symmetry versions of the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger and Benalcazar-Bernevig-Hughes models. These weak-symmetry models behave in many aspects just like their conventional brethren---in particular, they host robust edge states---, though the corresponding topological invariants are only \emph{approximately} quantized. We conclude this work by experimentally realizing Hermitian and non-Hermitian versions of such approximate topological insulators and probe their edge states. Overall, given the ubiquity of symmetry in all areas of physics and engineering, we foresee our work to serve as a cornerstone for exploring how conventional, strong symmetry requirements can be replaced by weak-symmetry ones.

items.title: Characterizing universal topological phases beyond spatial embedding
items.summary: Although Hamiltonians govern wave-matter interactions, conventional characterizations of topological phases of matter require more than the Hamiltonian alone, relying on global invariants defined on closed reciprocal-space manifolds or local commutation relations with position operators. This spatial dependence precludes a unique characterization of topological phases on an abstract platform, whose Hamiltonian can be defined independently of its spatial embedding. Here we establish a framework for characterizing universal topological phases, grounded in the invariance of topological features under arbitrary Hamiltonian-preserving deformations. We construct a Hamiltonian-based spatial embedding that groups a system's constituents according to their connectivity. This embedding, which reproduces the results of conventional topological diagnostics in established systems, enables a coherent extension of topological phases to complex networks using the Hamiltonian alone, further highlighting exceptional robustness in small-world networks. Our results reshape the conceptual foundations of topological physics by decoupling topological characterization from prescribed physical platforms.

items.title: Josephson effect in symmetry-mismatched van der Waals hybrid junctions of NbSe2-Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x and NbSe2-Bi2Sr2-xLaxCuO6+y
items.summary: Coupling superconductors of different symmetries may lead to emergent quantum phenomena but experimental studies on heterojunctions made of lattice-mismatched crystals are scarce. Here, we fabricate Josephson junction by van der Waals stacking NbSe2 flakes on freshly cleaved surfaces of Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x or Bi2Sr2-xLaxCuO6+y. We obtain pronounced Josephson currents across the heterojunctions at temperatures below 7 K. The Josephson coupling strength, characterized by the product of the critical Josephson current I_c and the normal state resistance R_n, can reach about 0.3 mV, much exceeding the values previously reported in Pb-Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x or Nb-Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x junctions. Microwave irradiation induces integer Shapiro steps. We also observe the Fraunhofer diffraction pattern by applying an in-plane magnetic field. We compare our results with the theoretical calculations that take into account the coherent tunneling and the order parameter mixing. Our work demonstrates the hybrid junctions as a distinctive platform for addressing pairing symmetry and emergent quantum phenomena.

items.title: Influence of embedding depth on the pullout of a plate from a confined granular medium
items.summary: Understanding the behaviour of moving objects within confined granular media is important in many technical applications. In this work we study the vertical pullout of a plate-like intruder buried at different depths within a dense granular aggregate from the onset of motion to flow around the intruder in the steady state by means of a two-dimensional polygonal Discrete Element Method. We find that the peak and steady-state drag forces depend differently on their embedding depth for different friction coefficients. Depending on the strength of friction the plate may interact with the domain walls, which enhances the drag force until failure of the aggregate, but not in the steady-state as dilation around intruder directs the force chains emanating from the plate upwards and away from the walls. If the inter-particle friction is weak, it is possible for the overhead pressure to overcome frictional resistance beyond a certain embedding depth. This prevents the formation of dilated failure zones above the intruder and changes the failure mode of the aggregate, leading to a slower decay of the steady-state drag forces with pullout distance.

items.title: Microscopic study of topological phase transitions: Percolation point of view
items.summary: We investigate microscopic mechanisms underlying decoherence-induced transitions between topologically ordered states. As a first case study, we analyze the color code using topological entanglement negativity (TEN) and a disorder parameter associated with 1-form symmetry. We interpret these quantities as first- and zeroth-dimensional simplicial homological objects, respectively, and show that the transition can be understood in terms of decoherence percolation. To resolve its local structure, we introduce quasi-local TEN (QLTEN), which visualizes the spatial distribution of local topological properties and the growth of decohered regions. We further introduce explosive percolation (EP), corresponding here to biased decoherence that suppresses the formation of large decohered clusters. As a second case study, we consider the toric code on a triangular lattice under external-field-type decoherence. Numerical results show that QLTEN faithfully captures the emergence of Higgs regions and the survival of logical qubits. Although global TEN, QLTEN clusters, and string operators are strongly correlated in both models, the color code and toric code respond differently to EP patterns. This difference indicates that a universal microscopic description of decoherence-induced topological phase transitions remains challenging even for closely related systems.
